title: Frontend: Word Search
businessContext: Build and verify the core behavior behind Word Search. This independently authored exercise has a bounded, explicit contract. Injected clock, network, random, or worker models are identified in the contract; they do not claim production service guarantees.
problemStatement: Implement solution({board,word}) using orthogonal adjacency with no cell reused per path. Board is rectangular code-point strings. Empty word returns true. Return a boolean without mutating board.
constraints: Define solution(input) in plain JavaScript. Return the documented JSON-compatible value or throw the documented validation error. Each case receives a fresh input.
Preserve identity, ordering, boundary behavior, and error messages stated in the contract. Passing fixtures verifies this contract, not every production concern.
candidateTasks: Implement the documented behavior without hard-coding fixture answers.
Run the full suite, investigate boundary failures, and explain the follow-up variation.
hints: Write down the state or algorithmic invariant, and trace the smallest boundary case before coding.
Start DFS/backtracking from each matching first character.
alternativeApproaches: Search many words with a trie to share prefixes and prune branches more effectively.
commonMistakes: Ignoring contract boundaries such as: Single character; repeated-letter path; reuse forbidden.
Treating a local deterministic model as proof of durable storage, authorization, distributed coordination, or physical-world guarantees.
